chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) met a slave of his on a cold night, and he was wearing a coat of khazz (fine wool), a turban of khazz, and a turban of khazz, and he was wrapped in Al-Ghaliya (a type of perfume). So he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! In a time like this, upon this attire, where are you going?' He said, 'To the mosque of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), to address the Maiden Hourie to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.الْحُورَ الْعِينَ: The Maiden Hourie (often used metaphorically for the soul or the believer addressing God)
key_terms.الْغَالِيَةِ: A type of perfume, often associated with luxury or specific ritual scents
key_terms.جُبَّةُ: A long outer garment or coat
key_terms.خَزٍّ: Fine wool or a specific type of fabric used for clothing
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ جَدِّي: The mosque of my grandfather (referring to the Prophet Muhammad SAWW)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'addressing the Maiden Hourie to Allah' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s balance between worldly dignity and spiritual devotion, as he wears luxurious wool and *Al-Ghaliya* perfume while heading to the Prophet’s Mosque. The phrase 'addressing the Maiden Hourie to Allah' employs the metaphor of a bride addressing her groom, illustrating the believer’s intimate, loving connection with the Divine. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that outward elegance can accompany inward humility when directed toward worship.
